title: The Use of Anomaly Detection for the Detection of Different Types of DDoS Attacks in Cloud Environment

publication.venue: Journal of Hardware and Systems Security

abstract: The accessible Springer preview associates the paper with a unified anomaly-detection approach for bandwidth-, application-, and connection-exhaustion DDoS groups, using CUSUM-style change detection and representative HTTP, database/application, and TCP SYN-flood attacks.

summary.core_contribution: The record identifies a cloud-DDoS anomaly-detection study that distinguishes multiple exhaustion-oriented attack types.
summary.problem: Cloud DDoS attacks can consume different resource layers and require detection methods that distinguish their behavioral signatures.
summary.method: The two-page preview describes one inclusive detector that compares normal and potential-attack traffic/resource behavior across bandwidth, application, and connection exhaustion, with CUSUM for change detection. It mentions representative HTTP, database/application, and TCP SYN-flood classes, but does not expose the complete toolchain, feature set, dataset protocol, or baselines.
summary.findings: The preview supports the attack-taxonomy and unified-detection framing, but exposes no sample counts, train/test protocol, hardware, detection rate, false-positive value, or other quantitative result.
summary.limitations: Only the official two-page Springer preview was accessible; the methods, experiments, references, limitations, and future-work section of the complete article remain unavailable.
summary.future_work: The paper-specific future-work section remains unverified because the complete article was not accessible.
